subject: Pilot: TTFT & sustained-token throughput carveout (Acme)
messages:
From: Ben Shaw <ben.shaw@acmetech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:15:00Z
Subject: Pilot: TTFT & sustained-token throughput carveout (Acme)

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team was impressed by Redwood's latency and the console traces. We're scoped to run a 6-week interactive pilot starting June 1 to validate an in-product conversational assistant for our enterprise customers. Before we lock in dates, I need to confirm whether Redwood can support two specific carveouts for the pilot:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) guarantees for streaming endpoints: our UX team requires p50 TTFT <= 300ms and p95 TTFT <= 600ms for interactive sessions under expected load.

2) Sustained token throughput per session: our average session expects ~45 tokens/sec sustained during longer completions (not burst), with spikes up to 80 tokens/sec for short periods. We expect up to 250 concurrent active sessions in the pilot (peak).

Given the nature of streaming and the mixed routing we saw in the demo, we want to request a formal carveout/exception to the standard hosted SLA that: (a) documents how TTFT is measured for streaming versus non-streaming endpoints, (b) specifies the measurement windows and rollback triggers, and (c) provides any pricing delta for the exception (if dedicated capacity or reserved throughput is required).

I'm attaching our traffic profile and a short table of session shapes. Can someone from Redwood confirm feasibility and propose a short mutually-agreeable acceptance criteria so we can move to contract? We can loop in our procurement/legal if needed.

Ben
Ben Shaw
Director, Product
Acme Tech

Attachments: Acme_traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Shaw <ben.shaw@acmetech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T10:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot: TTFT & sustained-token throughput carveout (Acme)

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear summary and the traffic profile. Looping in Rishi (inference/optimization) and Karthik (your AE) so we can align technical and commercial.

Quick read / proposed next steps from our side:
- Feasibility: on first pass this is doable with a Dedicated pool or a reserved burst band on Hosted. Streaming TTFT targets are highly sensitive to routing and KV-cache locality; we'd prefer to validate on a reserved pool for the pilot to avoid noisy-neighbor variance.
- Measurement definitions (proposal):
  * TTFT (streaming): time from request acceptance at ingress to the first token sent to the client. Window: p50/p95 measured across 60s rolling windows during business-hour load.
  * Sustained token/sec: average token emission rate per session measured over 30s windows, with an aggregated p95 across sessions used for capacity planning.
- Acceptance criteria (pilot):
  * p50 TTFT <= 250ms and p95 TTFT <= 550ms (we can tighten depending on test runs)
  * Sustained per-session average >= 35 tokens/sec sustained for 30s, with the ability to burst to 80 tokens/sec for <10% of requests.
  * Traffic shape validation via the attached CSV in two staged runs (week 1 load tests, week 3 production shadow).
- Commercial: if Acme prefers hosted with guaranteed routing we will price a reserved throughput band; Dedicated pool pricing available with predictable latency SLOs. Karthik will provide a delta estimate.

Rishi — Can you confirm the test harness (we have an internal streaming harness) and the telemetry we need (TTFT logs, stream chunk timestamps, kv-cache hit rates)? Also note we will need to define rollback triggers (e.g., sustained p95 TTFT breach > 30 minutes or error-rate spike).

Ben — if this direction sounds acceptable we'll draft a short SLA exception and circulate to legal. Karthik, please add the pricing delta and any operational runbook (oncall, escalation path).

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
m: +1 415-555-0143

Subject: Re: Pilot: TTFT & sustained-token throughput carveout (Acme)

Monica — thanks, that framing helps. Couple clarifications from our engineering lead:
- We actually need per-session sustained average closer to 45 tokens/sec (not 35). That's our baseline for the assistant to feel responsive on long exchanges.
- For TTFT we care most about p95 during business hours (UTC-8). The p50 is useful but p95 is the gating metric for the UX team.

I've attached a redline the legal team drafted that proposes wording for the carveout. Can you have Redwood's legal/ops take a quick look? We need to lock language and pricing before the May 20 purchase committee meeting.

Ben

Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. Forwarding a short draft SLA exception that captures the measurement windows, rollback triggers, and a pricing delta for reserved throughput. I pulled the language conservative enough for legal but flexible operationally so we can iterate after the staged load runs.

On Fri, May 13, 2027 at 17:02 Ben Shaw <ben.shaw@acmetech.com> wrote:
> Monica — thanks, that framing helps. Couple clarifications from our engineering lead:
> - We actually need per-session sustained average closer to 45 tokens/sec (not 35). That's our baseline for the assistant to feel responsive on long exchanges.
> - For TTFT we care most about p95 during business hours (UTC-8). The p50 is useful but p95 is the gating metric for the UX team.

Draft highlights (attached):
- Scope: streaming endpoints used by Acme's interactive assistant (endpoint ids enumerated in appendix). Non-streaming (sync) endpoints remain bound to the standard hosted SLA.
- Measurement: TTFT = ingress acceptance -> first token sent. Measured p50/p95 over rolling 60s windows during business hours; token-rate measured over 30s windows.
- Triggers: A sustained p95 TTFT breach > 20 mins triggers rollback to standard routing or capacity increase; crediting formula in appendix.
- Pricing: reserved throughput band priced as a monthly add-on; option to move to Dedicated pool at a capped delta.

Next steps: Karthik to provide the commercial delta and an MSA addendum; Rishi to confirm the telemetry events and schema we'll include in the acceptance tests. If Acme legal can send redlines against the attached sla_exception_draft.pdf we'll aim to have a final by May 19.

Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
